reviews.body: **Devin Review** found 4 potential issues.

The existing review threads identify real compatibility issues, and I independently confirmed two more request-shape details. With the supported minimum anthropic==0.18.0, the published Messages.create signature has extra_body but no thinking keyword; binding the new helper output fails with TypeError: unexpected keyword argument thinking. Please either send thinking via extra_body at synchronous call sites (keeping batch params native), or raise and test the SDK minimum. Also, selecting the newly advertised claude-sonnet-5-5 memory answer model captures temperature=0.0 in both the answer and default LiteLLM judge requests; please omit unsupported sampling parameters and verify routing for both. The before/after proxy comparison still omits the direct arm’s thinking policy, so it needs a parity regression as well. These are local signature/request-capture checks, not live Anthropic results. Please include the required optional-integration mypy and owner regression proof.

<!-- headroom-agentops:9238f1dd39cf89461c2e330e697baf5af08ac1247784ae8a0d25b6c1c87c0b2b -->

review_comments.body: 🔍 **Required eval integration verification gap** The PR reports targeted tests but no `mypy headroom` run. The [optional-integration checks](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/CONTRIBUTING.md "CONTRIBUTING.md") require it with the relevant extra installed. --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔴 **Default eval failure on supported SDKs** On Anthropic SDK 0.18.0, `anthropic_thinking_kwargs` produces a keyword that `messages.create` rejects before sending the request. The [evals extra](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/pyproject.toml#L310-L317 "pyproject.toml:310-317") still accepts that SDK, so default quick and batch runs fail without scoring any answers.
Learn more The [quick runner](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/evals/runners/before_after.py#L529-L554 "headroom/evals/runners/before_after.py:529-554") selects Sonnet 5.5 and calls [the Anthropic client](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/evals/runners/before_after.py#L187-L194 "headroom/evals/runners/before_after.py:187-194"). The [batch evaluator](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/evals/batch_compression_eval.py#L1057-L1066 "headroom/evals/batch_compression_eval.py:1057-1066") and [memory judge](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/evals/memory/judge.py#L134-L149 "headroom/evals/memory/judge.py:134-149") expand the same helper into their calls. Anthropic SDK 0.18.0 meets the [evals dependency requirement](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/pyproject.toml#L310-L317 "pyproject.toml:310-317"), but its `messages.create` method accepts `extra_body`, not a top-level `thinking` keyword. The [new test double](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/tests/test_evals_anthropic_default_model.py#L13-L25 "tests/test_evals_anthropic_default_model.py:13-25") accepts arbitrary keyword arguments, so it cannot catch the rejection. **Example:** Run `python -m headroom.evals quick -n 1` with Anthropic SDK 0.18.0 installed. Both model calls fail locally before contacting Anthropic, and the CLI reports failed accuracy preservation. **Recommended fix:** Pass the native Messages API `thinking` field through `extra_body` at SDK call sites while keeping it at the top level of batch `params`. Test the wire payload through a real SDK client at the supported minimum.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🔴 **Advertised memory model rejects answer requests** Selecting the advertised Sonnet 5.5 model makes [_run_memory_eval](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/cli/evals.py#L516-L522 "headroom/cli/evals.py:516-522") send `temperature=0.0` through LiteLLM. Sonnet 5.5 rejects that setting, and the answer error stops the memory evaluation. The default [LiteLLM judge](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/evals/memory/judge.py#L188-L193 "headroom/evals/memory/judge.py:188-193") also sends it when reusing the answer model.
Learn more The CLI passes `--answer-model` to [_run_memory_eval](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/cli/evals.py#L481-L522 "headroom/cli/evals.py:481-522"), which sends every question with retrieved memories to LiteLLM with `temperature=0.0`. Sonnet 5.5 rejects that value. When LiteLLM recognizes the model, either its adapter rejects the parameter or Anthropic rejects the request. The locked LiteLLM version also lacks this model in its bundled lookup table, so the bare name depends on an updated table for provider inference. [The memory evaluator](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/evals/memory/runner.py "headroom/evals/memory/runner.py") does not catch answer generation errors, and [judge selection](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/cli/evals.py#L528-L543 "headroom/cli/evals.py:528-543") reuses the answer model by default. **Example:** Run `headroom evals memory --answer-model claude-sonnet-5-5` with an Anthropic key. The first question with retrieved memories fails instead of producing an answer. With `--llm-judge`, fixing only the answer request leaves the default LiteLLM judge sending the same unsupported setting. **Recommended fix:** Route Sonnet 5.5 answers and judging through a compatible Anthropic adapter, or configure both LiteLLM calls to route the model explicitly and omit unsupported sampling parameters. Exercise the advertised command with the supported dependency versions before documenting the model.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Mismatched thinking in proxy comparisons** For proxied Sonnet 5.5 requests, `_call_llm_via_proxy` leaves default thinking enabled on upstreams that honor Anthropic’s defaults. The [direct baseline](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/evals/runners/before_after.py#L187-L194 "headroom/evals/runners/before_after.py:187-194") disables up-front thinking. The benchmark compares different reasoning settings as well as different compression paths.
Learn more [Before/after evaluation](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/evals/runners/before_after.py#L330-L349 "headroom/evals/runners/before_after.py:330-349") sends the original prompt directly and, when a proxy client is configured, sends it through Headroom for compression. The [direct Anthropic call](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom/blob/8401dcc97e6dd3b2f799b6a51844b4122e015f53/headroom/evals/runners/before_after.py#L187-L194 "headroom/evals/runners/before_after.py:187-194") selects `between_tools`, which turns off up-front thinking. The proxy call omits any corresponding setting, so an upstream that honors Anthropic’s defaults spends part of the same output budget on adaptive thinking. Its answer can differ even when the proxy does not change the prompt. **Example:** Run a full-stack comparison against Sonnet 5.5 with an Anthropic-compatible upstream that defaults to adaptive thinking. Even a case whose prompt the proxy leaves untouched is compared with up-front thinking off in one arm and on in the other. **Recommended fix:** For Anthropic-backed comparisons, send the same native Messages payload through both the direct and proxied clients, or use a proxy mapping verified to preserve the same thinking mode. Add a test comparing the effective settings in both arms.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*
